RIFT DUEL / BALANCE LAB

Tune fighters, moves and shared rules, and watch frame advantage, playstyle and matchups update live. Starting values are read from the game's code (dist/balance/roster.json, regenerated by npm run balance:extract). Yellow cells differ from the code. Frame advantage is estimated from the shared constants, about ±2 frames.

New fighter

The new fighter copies every stat and move from the template. Then tune it like any other.
■ startup ■ active ■ recovery · Block / Hit: + means the attacker moves first · Open: frames stuck after contact or a miss (active − 1 + recovery).
Base damage is before the fighter's power multiplier; multi-hit moves are summed. Block and hit are blank where they depend on distance (projectiles, areas, grabs).

Roster balance

Six scores from 0 to 100 on fixed scales, so new fighters compare fairly. Budget is their average. The tick on each bar is the roster average. The playstyle label is what the numbers say, shown beside the intended style.

Live checks

Matchup grid

Rows whiff, columns punish. Top line: reach gap (green, the row fighter outreaches). Below: if the row fighter whiffs Strike 1 at max reach, can the column fighter close in and punish in time, with the reaction time on the Game rules tab? Outlined cells are punishable on reaction.

Game rules

Shared timings that apply to every fighter. Changing one updates every table.

Changes from the code

Everything you changed, written as a task for Codex with the source file each value lives in. Export saves the tuning as JSON in the format the hosted Rift Duel Frame Codex uses, so the two can trade files.

Remove every change and new fighter? 

 
Playing tuned values at normal speed needs an opt-in simulation switch that loads these overrides (proposed for Codex as &balance=local). This lab only computes from the constants; it never changes the game.
